passage: Last year I noticed that everything had gone grey. Work was fine, family was fine, but I woke up tired and nothing interested me. I'm Baljeet, and at first I just waited it out. Mentor's note, working women's hostel, Pune

Jyoti came to me in January saying life felt 'flat and grey'. Work, hostel, phone, sleep. Not sad, she said, just dull. Her friend Pooja had noticed too. Together we made a small plan. Sister Agnes, hostel mentor

Your sister,
Minakshi

Week three. Himani still couldn't sleep. She cried quietly into her pillow one night and thought nobody heard. The next morning Elizabeth said, 'I miss my mum's cooking too. It's awful, isn't it?' Himani stared. 'You too?'

Week five. The two of them made a list of home foods on the dorm wall. They told the warden they were homesick, and she arranged a Sunday phone call for them both. Himani still missed home. But she slept better.
